title: Exchange "price lock" needing card details vs. exchange pickup scheduled with no payment
summary: The recipient ordered a new Voltrix phone on ShopKart with an exchange offer on their old phone. A caller from the "ShopKart exchange team" phones before delivery. In the legitimate case, the agent confirms the old phone's model and condition, schedules the exchange pickup at the time of delivery, and says nothing more is payable because the difference was paid at checkout. In the fraud case, the caller says the exchange value must be "locked" with a refundable hold on the recipient's card and asks for the full card number, expiry date, and CVV. This family shares the card-details evidence type with `ec_09`, but differs in initiation (outbound, not recipient-initiated) and pretext (a pending exchange, not a delayed refund). Both cases mention the card, the exchange value, and the price difference.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: the ShopKart customer who placed the order; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Exchange value of the old phone: [AMOUNT_18] (₹2,000–₹15,000); the price difference was paid by card at checkout.
Both callers know the order, the old phone model, and the exchange value.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller asks for full card credentials, including CVV, on a call to "lock" an exchange value. The payment was already made at checkout, and no genuine entity asks for CVV on a call.
fraud.caller_objective: Obtain card credentials, then the OTP, to make a purchase.
stable_facts: The caller says exchange prices "change daily" and the offer lapses tonight unless locked.
The caller says the hold is "refundable" and "not a charge".
The caller asks for the details verbally; no link is sent.

legitimate.label_rationale: The agent confirms exchange details and schedules the pickup with delivery. The recipient is told no further payment or card detail is needed.
legitimate.caller_objective: Make sure the exchange pickup goes smoothly at delivery.
stable_facts: The agent asks simple condition questions: does the old phone switch on, is the screen cracked.
The exchange value is fixed at checkout and shown on the order page; the delivery agent checks the old phone at the door.
If the old phone fails the check, the recipient can pay the difference in the app or cancel the exchange at the door.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may press about the deadline or ask for the OTP that follows the card details (same mechanism). They must not switch to links, UPI requests, or app installation. The legitimate agent must not ask for card details, codes, or any payment.

must_preserve: exchange value and "card" in both cases
card number, expiry, and CVV request in _F
condition questions and no-payment statement in _L
may_vary: old and new phone models (Voltrix range only)

ambiguities: Real exchange programmes can re-price an old phone at the door; in this family that happens only through the app or by cancelling, never by card details on a call.
Card" appears in _L (the difference was charged to it) as a confound.
If generation has the caller ask only for the "last four digits", the prefix is not eligible for _F.

evidence_references.claim: Genuine entities never ask for card details, CVV, or OTP (C01)
Impostors cite urgency to obtain card details (C02)
A major marketplace never asks for payment information over the phone (CE13, CE14)
